headline: Federal Parkway Regulations and Service Limits
reservation: The Parkway itself has no entry fees or permits, but campgrounds like Jeff Busby or Rocky Springs operate on changing federal systems. There are no hotels directly on the road; accommodation must be booked in gateway cities like Tupelo or Natchez. Always verify campground status via official National Park Service alerts.

days.title: Tennessee Valleys and Frontier History

stops.name: Natchez Trace Parkway Bridge
stops.detail: Stop at Milepost 438 for the double-arched view of the Tennessee hills.

stops.name: Meriwether Lewis Site
stops.detail: Visit the monument and reconstructed cabin marking the site of the explorer’s final journey.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours; the 50mph speed limit is strictly enforced
days.note: Fuel is not available on the Parkway; you must exit to local towns for all services.

days.title: Ancient Mounds and Civil War Echoes
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Tupelo Visitor Center

stops.name: Pharr Mounds
stops.detail: Explore the 90-acre site containing eight ancient burial mounds dating back two thousand years.

stops.name: Confederate Gravesites
stops.detail: A short walk to a somber clearing where thirteen unknown soldiers were interred.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours; stop frequently for historical markers
days.note: Mississippi humidity can be high; plan short hikes for the cooler morning hours.

days.title: Swamps and Sunken Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Jackson or nearby gateway

stops.name: Cypress Swamp
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk over dark waters filled with water tupelo and bald cypress trees.

stops.name: Sunken Trace
stops.detail: Experience the deeply eroded original path worn down by centuries of travelers at Milepost 41.5.

days.driving: Allow 2–3 hours; winding sections require focus
days.note: Watch for wildlife like wild turkey and deer crossing the road at dawn and dusk.

days.title: Ceremonial Earthworks and River Bluffs

stops.name: Emerald Mound
stops.detail: Climb one of the largest Mississippian era mounds in North America for a panoramic view.

stops.name: Natchez Under-the-Hill
stops.detail: Conclude the journey at the historic riverfront where the Trace met the Mississippi River.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours; road conditions are typically excellent but watch for fallen debris
days.note: Stay off restricted mound surfaces to preserve these sacred indigenous landmarks.

intel.title: Scenic Overlook Capacity
intel.text: Most interpretive stops have small paved lots that rarely fill completely. Larger RVs should use designated pull-outs to avoid blocking smaller trailhead access.

intel.title: Remote Communication
intel.text: Cellular service is notoriously spotty between Milepost 100 and 300. Download offline navigation and notify others of your itinerary before entering the Parkway.

intel.title: Off-Parkway Services
intel.text: Signage indicates distances to towns like Clinton or Tupelo for gas. Always exit for fuel when your tank reaches a quarter, as distances between exits can be deceptive.

intel.title: Optimal Drive Pacing
intel.text: Avoid driving after dark due to high wildlife activity and a lack of road lighting. A 50mph pace allows for safe stopping when sightings occur.

intel.title: Trail Maintenance
intel.text: Swamp boardwalks may close temporarily after heavy rains. Check the official NPS 'Conditions' page for bridge closures or trail washouts.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Nashville or MSL airport; stock a cooler with water and food as there are no concessions on the Parkway.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are ideal; cyclists are frequent, so check mirror clearance. RVs must be aware of limited turning radii at some smaller historic markers.
plan.goldenHour: Little Mountain Overlook for a high-elevation view of the Mississippi forest at dusk.
